NUZZLE.summary: Moves the caster to a free cell next to an enemy chosen by Board.getFarthestTargetCoordinateAvailablePlace (usually far from the caster, but NOT guaranteed to be the farthest enemy: see targeting), retargets to that enemy, then paralyses it and deals special damage. If the helper returns null the caster stays and hits the cast target.

targeting.who: the enemy attached to the helper's selected cell: scanning enemies in board order, each enemy whose distance is STRICTLY greater than the running maximum updates the maximum and, only if it has at least one free adjacent cell, replaces the selected destination (and its enemy). The cast target is replaced by that enemy.
targeting.note: Cases (read from the helper, not executed): (1) normal: the last maximum-setting enemy that has a free adjacent cell is chosen, with the free adjacent cell farthest from the caster (first such cell on ties). (2) RETAINED SELECTION: if an enemy that sets a new maximum distance has no free adjacent cell, the earlier selectedCell is kept (it is never cleared) and its enemy - nearer than the farthest - becomes the target. (3) because the running maximum was already raised, enemies scanned later at a distance <= that maximum are skipped, even if they are nearer than the farthest enemy but farther than the retained one, and even if they have free cells. (4) FALLBACK: only if no enemy at all produced a selected cell, the free cell closest to the last-recorded 'farthest' enemy (getClosestAvailablePlace) is used with that enemy as target. (5) if that also fails (or no targettable enemy exists) the helper returns null: the caster does not move and the original cast target is hit. Ties in distance keep the first enemy in scan order (strict >). The scan order of board.forEach and the exact distanceM metric were not read.

geometry.shape: single target; caster relocates to the free adjacent cell (of the selected enemy) that is farthest from the caster, first on ties; unchanged if no cell is returned

DRAGON_RAGE.summary: Gives the caster an initial shield and starts a 6-pulse effect: each pulse (every 1000 timer units) adds more shield and hits all adjacent enemies with special damage; when the effect ends, C = min(current shield, tracked raw shield) is removed from the shield and 40 % of C (rounded) is requested as healing.

effects.condition: each pulse, to every enemy on an adjacent cell
effects.scaling: AP: x(1 + AP/100) (no apBoost argument => handleSpecialDamage default true); crit only if the cast itself crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT), and that crit flag is stored in the effect at creation
effects.resolution: then SPE_DEF division per pulse, ceil, min 1, and later modifiers

effects.condition: once on the first cast (initial) and once per pulse
effects.scaling: addShield(value, caster, apBoost 1, crit): x(1 + AP/100), x critPower if the cast crit, halved if the unit is enraged, rounded; Big Eater Belt hook in PokemonEntity.addShield
effects.resolution: the amount actually received can exceed (AP) or fall below (enrage) the raw value, while the stored counter `shieldGiven` adds the RAW value only

declaredRaw.formula: removes C shield; requests healing round(0.4 x C), where C = min(current shield, shieldGiven)
declaredRaw.note: removed shield (C) and requested healing (0.4 x C, rounded) are different amounts. shieldGiven = raw initial shield + raw per-pulse shields added since the effect (or since the last conversion) started

perUnitRaw.GYARADOS: C = 135 gives 135 shield removed and a base healing request of round(0.4 x 135) = 54 (before healing modifiers); other values of C give other amounts

effects.scaling: the healing request is not AP- or crit-scaled (handleHeal called with apBoost 0, crit false), but handleHeal then applies its own modifiers: wound => 0, burn x0.5, enraged x0.5, BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED x1.3, zenith weather x1.2, rounding, cap at missing HP. The 54 is the BASE request, not a universal maximum: modifiers can raise or lower the healing received, and C itself varies (damage taken, recast, enrage)
effects.resolution: C depends on how much of the tracked shield is still on the unit; the removal is an exchange (shield lost) while the healing request is 40 % of it; actual healing received is whatever handleHeal returns

DRAGON_RAGE.positionalConditions: None for casting. Damage depends on which enemies are on the 8 adjacent cells at each pulse.
DRAGON_RAGE.repeatedCastsAndModes: State: a DragonRageEffect with ticksRemaining (6) and shieldGiven. FIRST cast: adds the initial shield and creates the effect. CAST WHILE ACTIVE: no new initial shield is added; the active effect converts its tracked shield into healing right away (consumeShield) and ticksRemaining is reset to 6 (the effect's 1000-unit timer is not reset). The effect ends on the pulse where ticksRemaining would go below 0, i.e. after 6 damaging pulses the 7th timer fire ends it and converts what is left. Each cast still spends maxPP of PP.
DRAGON_RAGE.rawVsResolved: Declared raw for 3 stars: initial shield 45, per pulse shield 15 and damage 15, 6 pulses; tracked raw shield 45 + 6 x 15 = 135. With C = 135 (all tracked shield still present at the end) the conversion removes 135 shield and requests round(0.4 x 135) = 54 healing as the BASE request, before handleHeal's modifiers (burn/enrage halve, wound zeroes, BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED x1.3, zenith x1.2) and the cap at missing HP. Actual shield received includes AP scaling and may be lower after damage, so C can be smaller; it can never exceed the tracked raw counter.
